summary: New Hampshire is one of the most clearly favorable states: its Fish & Game rule N.H. Admin. Code Fis 804.02(b)(7) names 'Rats, domesticated (Rattus norvegicus and Rattus rattus)' as NON-CONTROLLED wildlife — by binomial — meaning no permit is required to possess, breed, or import a captive-bred roof rat. (The rule was re-adopted effective 2026-04-20 with the listing unchanged.) Selling is unobstructed from the Fish & Game side; the only touchpoint is the Dept of Agriculture's 'pet vendor' license, a threshold-triggered business registration for selling small mammals at volume (free transfers can count toward the threshold). Never release one — that's the single firm prohibition.

keep.why: N.H. Admin. Code Fis 804.02(a) requires no permit to possess non-controlled wildlife, and Fis 804.02(b)(7) lists 'Rats, domesticated (Rattus norvegicus and Rattus rattus)' as non-controlled — both species named. RSA 207:1 also defines 'wild animals' as all animals other than domestic, reinforcing that a captive-bred domestic rat needs no permit.
keep.governing_law: N.H. Admin. Code Fis 804.02(b)(7); RSA 207:1; RSA 207:14.

breed.why: Non-controlled designation covers breeding (possession encompasses progeny); the propagation permit (Fis 806) applies to controlled/prohibited wildlife, not non-controlled species. Hobby/non-commercial breeding needs no Fish & Game permit. Breeding for sale at volume may bring the Dept of Agriculture pet-vendor license into play (see sell_give).
breed.governing_law: N.H. Admin. Code Fis 804.02(b)(7); Fis 806; RSA 437:1.

sell_give.why: No Fish & Game sale permit applies to non-controlled mammals (Fis 811 covers indigenous herps only). The Dept of Agriculture 'pet vendor' license (RSA 437; Agr 1701) is required to transfer small mammals 'to the public' above a threshold quantity set by rule — and RSA 437:1 counts transfers 'with or without a fee or donation,' so high-volume free adoption can count. Below the threshold, selling/giving is unregulated.

transport.why: No Fish & Game import permit is required for non-controlled species (Fis 803). Imported animals must meet Dept of Agriculture (Agr 2100), USDA-APHIS, and USFWS rules; Agr 2100's CVI list enumerates livestock categories, not pet rodents, and APHIS has no interstate health-cert requirement for pet rodents — so no CVI is clearly required (confirm with the State Vet). Releasing R. rattus into the wild is prohibited (Fis 805 / RSA 207:14).
transport.governing_law: N.H. Admin. Code Fis 803; Fis 804.02(b)(7); Agr 2100; Fis 805 / RSA 207:14 (no-release).

restrictions.summary: Transferring small mammals 'to the public' above the Dept of Agriculture's threshold (Agr 1701.02; counts free transfers too) requires a NH pet-vendor license — a routine business registration, not a species restriction. Confirm the small-mammal threshold with the Division of Animal Industry.
steps: Confirm the Agr 1701.02 small-mammal threshold; register as a pet vendor if you exceed it
restrictions.where_to_file: NH Dept of Agriculture, Markets & Food — Division of Animal Industry

restrictions.summary: Never release a roof rat into the wild (Fis 805 / RSA 207:14). Check local ordinances.
